item.title: AI executive calls OpenAI hacking event a wake-up call for the industry
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Thomas Wolf, co-founder and chief science officer for Hugging Face, an AI company, discusses the recent hacking incident involving ChatGPT.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Thomas Wolf, co-founder and chief science officer for Hugging Face, an AI company, discusses the recent hacking incident involving ChatGPT.

item.title: Allegations of AI distillation spark debate about IP theft. But is it illegal?
item.description: Distillation lets AI companies train new models using existing ones. The White House says Chinese firms are using it to gain an edge, raising questions about competition and intellectual property.
item.content:encoded: Distillation lets AI companies train new models using existing ones. The White House says Chinese firms are using it to gain an edge, raising questions about competition and intellectual property.
item.dc:creator: John Ruwitch

item.title: AI tokens could become the kilowatt-hour of the AI age
item.description: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.
item.content:encoded: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.

item.title: Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5B Anthropic copyright infringement ruling
item.description: Some say the $3,100 per title payout is small compensation for what they view as big, ongoing threats from the makers of generative AI models.

item.title: Sony says it will stop producing physical discs for PlayStation games
item.description: Sony's Playstation games once ran solely on discs. But with advances in technology, physical discs are unnecessary, and the company will soon stop making them.

item.title: OpenAI says AI models hacked into another AI company without being instructed
item.description: NPR's A Martinez asks Nate Soares of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute how two experimental OpenAI models hacked their way onto the internet and into another AI company, without instruction.
